candidates.name: Job Objects
verified_facts: Job objects manage groups of processes as a unit and can be nested on supported systems
A process may be associated with job constraints inherited through nesting
semantic_limits: Job membership is not proof of task identity or receipt publication

candidates.name: IsProcessInJob
verified_facts: IsProcessInJob tests whether a process is in a specified job or any job
The process handle needs query rights and the job handle needs query rights when supplied
semantic_limits: A false result can reflect access failure unless function success and GetLastError are recorded

candidates.name: QueryInformationJobObject
verified_facts: QueryInformationJobObject retrieves accounting, limits, process lists, and other job state
A null job handle can query the immediate job of the calling process
semantic_limits: Query results are point-in-time and require buffer-length and return-length validation

candidates.name: JOBOBJECT_BASIC_PROCESS_ID_LIST
verified_facts: The structure reports assigned-process count and process IDs returned in the buffer
Nested jobs can contribute process IDs to the list
semantic_limits: A truncated list must be retried; each PID requires start-time correlation

candidates.name: JOBOBJECT_BASIC_ACCOUNTING_INFORMATION
verified_facts: The structure contains aggregate user/kernel time and process-count accounting for a job
Total and active process counts are distinct
semantic_limits: Aggregate accounting cannot identify which process produced a receipt

candidates.name: JOBOBJECT_BASIC_AND_IO_ACCOUNTING_INFORMATION
verified_facts: The structure combines basic job accounting with I/O counters
I/O aggregates can indicate activity changes across samples
semantic_limits: I/O deltas do not prove forward progress or receipt validity

candidates.name: JOBOBJECT_EXTENDED_LIMIT_INFORMATION
verified_facts: The structure includes basic limits, I/O information, and memory-limit fields
Limit flags determine which fields are active
semantic_limits: Reading limits must not be followed by mutation in this recovery-only package

candidates.name: JOBOBJECT_LIMIT_VIOLATION_INFORMATION_2
verified_facts: The structure reports job limit thresholds and current or accumulated violation information
Violation fields are meaningful only for enabled notification limits
semantic_limits: A violation can explain throttling but does not prove the runner is the affected owner

candidates.name: GetFileInformationByHandleEx
verified_facts: GetFileInformationByHandleEx retrieves selected information classes for an open file handle
The requested class determines the output structure and required buffer size
semantic_limits: The handle must refer to the intended file and must not be replaced by path-only evidence

candidates.name: FILE_ID_INFO
verified_facts: FILE_ID_INFO combines a volume serial number and 128-bit file identifier
The pair can distinguish whether two open handles refer to the same file on one computer
semantic_limits: File identity does not prove unchanged bytes; cryptographic hashes remain required

candidates.name: GetFileInformationByHandle
verified_facts: GetFileInformationByHandle returns BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION for a file handle
Network-backed files can return partial information or fail depending on server support
semantic_limits: Partial network information must not be promoted to stable local-file identity

candidates.name: BY_HANDLE_FILE_INFORMATION
verified_facts: The structure includes volume serial number, file size, link count, timestamps, and file index
Volume serial plus file index can identify a file on a volume
semantic_limits: Legacy file index width and remote-filesystem behavior require explicit caveats

candidates.name: GetFinalPathNameByHandleW
verified_facts: GetFinalPathNameByHandle returns the final path associated with a file handle
Flags control DOS, GUID, NT, or no-volume path formatting
semantic_limits: Equivalent files can have multiple path representations; handle identity remains primary

candidates.name: GetVolumeInformationW
verified_facts: GetVolumeInformation returns volume name, serial number, filesystem name, and capability flags
Filesystem flags describe supported behaviors such as persistent ACLs or reparse points
semantic_limits: Volume capabilities do not prove the specific receipt write was durable
